annotation.material_differences: Response C adds a stronger claim that the shared calculation change will 'keep the reports aligned with the new logic' and frames limitation as only for later complaints, while A and B explicitly acknowledge the cause is not yet confirmed and are more tentative. More importantly, none of the responses satisfies the 'cause identification' criterion in the same way; A and B explicitly proceed without pinning down the actual cause, and C also does not identify a supported cause. The shift in how confidently the correction is tied to a cause and justified could affect criterion-level evidence, especially for linked correction and correction justification.
annotation.equivalence_rationale: All three responses prefer changing the shared calculation component over limiting functionality, so they preserve the broad correction direction. However, they do not preserve the same decision-relevant evidence under the criteria because they all lack a supported cause identification, and C adds a somewhat stronger, more prescriptive justification for the change than A and B. Since the evaluation is about whether the responses preserve criterion-level evidence, this difference is material rather than merely stylistic.
